description: I have a background in aerospace engineering and a strong interest in astrophysics, space exploration, and scientific research. I am currently developing SPHEREx RELIC, an interactive web tool for exploring changes in real NASA SPHEREx observations using an experimental adaptive-memory approach. I am participating individually in this challenge.
summary:
SPHEREx RELIC is an interactive web-based prototype designed to help people explore changes in the infrared sky using real NASA SPHEREx observations.

The application presents two observations of the same sky region, separated by approximately 38 days. Users can compare the images, adjust contrast, switch visualization modes, and examine a normalized difference map.

Its experimental RELIC detector introduces a bounded adaptive-memory approach that uses information from a previous observation to help identify potential changes. Users can compare memory-enabled and memory-disabled detector responses and explore candidate locations using adjustable display thresholds.

The project combines publicly accessible astronomical data, interactive visualization, and an experimental change-detection method in a retro-futuristic interface.

This demonstration uses one selected sky region. Candidate detections are exploratory and have not been independently confirmed as astronomical transients. Future development could extend the tool to additional sky regions and observations.
details:
SPHEREx RELIC — Research and Exploration of Localized Infrared Changes

SPHEREx RELIC is a research prototype designed to identify and evaluate subtle signals in astronomical observations using NASA SPHEREx data.

The project explores whether adaptive, information-based analysis can improve the detection of faint sources and localized changes that may be difficult to distinguish from observational noise.

How does it work?

RELIC analyzes astronomical image data using a combination of signal detection, statistical calibration, and adaptive information-based methods. It compares candidate signals against noise-only conditions and evaluates their reliability through controlled injection and recovery experiments.

What makes it innovative?

RELIC explores an alternative to conventional signal detection by incorporating adaptive relationships within observational data. Its design draws on selected concepts from an independently developed theoretical framework without requiring disclosure of the underlying research.

Development and testing

The prototype was developed in Python using scientific computing and numerical analysis tools. Testing included real astronomical image data, synthetic signal injections, false-positive calibration, and comparisons with conventional matched-filter detection.

Expected impact

RELIC aims to provide researchers and citizen scientists with an accessible approach to investigating weak astronomical signals in SPHEREx observations.

The project is experimental. Its current results demonstrate a working research and validation pipeline, while broader improvements in detection performance require further testing.

Future development

The next stage is to integrate the validated detection pipeline into an interactive web interface, enabling users to explore observational data, inspect candidate detections, and understand their statistical significance.
